ws review checks a review document — one JSON object: a verdict, a
summary, a profile, and comments carrying an id you choose, a priority, a
category, a body, anchors, and competing suggestions.

Read the shape before writing one:

ws review describe          the document shape
ws review describe --list   every name it can explain

Run inside your review workspace, and don't change its checkout: submit
verifies every anchor against its repository at the commit under review.
Anchor paths are repo-relative. Leave ref out — ws fills in the reviewed
commit — and set profile to the one you were primed with.

The loop:

1. Write the review.
2. ws review submit --json -   (stdin; or a path)
3. Read the JSON, not prose. Exit 0: stored, done.
4. Exit 1, review_invalid: error.details lists each diagnostic, named by
   its check, and "lenses" — run ws review describe --lens=a,b,c, fix,
   resubmit. One call reports every fault it can, so fix them all before
   you resubmit. Only review_invalid retries.
5. Exit 1, review_unverifiable: the checkout diverged from the commit or
   lacks it. Exit 2: fix the invocation. Exit 3: not a review workspace.
   These stop: report them.
6. Unsure about a field? ws review describe --lens=<field>. Never guess at
   an enum or a scale.

Advisories report review quality and never fail the run; structural and
anchor errors do. Resubmitting under your profile replaces your earlier
submission.
